profile: Designs, builds and sells electric cars, pickup trucks and battery storage systems. It also earns revenue from leasing, used cars, repairs, charging, insurance, software subscriptions, solar products and regulatory credits.

otherClaims.label: Debt and other claims, less cash

summary: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA, NASDAQ Global Select) designs, builds and sells electric cars, pickup trucks and battery storage systems, alongside leasing, charging, insurance, software and regulatory-credit activities. The share price was 397 USD on 27 October 2026, giving equity value of USD 1.57tn and enterprise value of USD 1.58tn. Cars and Energy are established businesses; Robotaxi and Optimus have barely started selling. The valuation therefore separates operating businesses with analysts’ forecasts from the growth that must come from new activities. The whole company carries 2026 forecast EV/EBIT of 277x, falling to 143x on 2028 forecast operating profit of USD 11,026m.

The share price assigns 9 USD per share to Cars and 4 USD per share to Energy, less 2 USD per share for debt and other claims, less cash. Cars implies 3.6x 2028 operating profit of USD 9,541m, while Energy implies 10.4x 2028 operating profit of USD 1,485m. Robotaxi carries 309 USD per share and needs USD 1.62tn of 2040 sales at a 25% operating margin, or USD 404bn of operating profit. Optimus carries 77 USD per share and needs USD 445bn of 2040 sales at a 20% margin, or USD 89.1bn of operating profit.

Cars is priced at the same 2028 EV/EBIT multiple as General Motors at 3.6x and Ford at 3.7x, while Energy is in line with BYD at 10.4x and below its peer median of 11.4x. The decisive reading rests on whether Robotaxi reaches fleet scale, annual sales of USD 1.62tn and 25% margins, and whether Optimus finds outside customers by the end of 2027. Nearer-term evidence includes Q3 deliveries of 486,532 vehicles, automotive gross margin of 18.5%, Energy revenue of USD 2,881m and storage deployment of 13.7 GWh.

thesis.title: Profit required
thesis.text: A 397 USD share needs the whole company to reach USD 2.41tn of sales and USD 519bn of operating profit by 2040, a 22% margin. Analysts forecast USD 147bn of sales and USD 11bn of operating profit for 2028, leaving the share price dependent on substantial new-business profit.

thesis.title: Robotaxi execution
thesis.text: Robotaxi needs USD 1.62tn of 2040 sales, 1.6 times Goldman Sachs’s USD 415bn forecast for the worldwide market in 2035. Tesla has nearly 2 million unsupervised miles, but only 42 authorised Texas vehicles in May 2026 versus Waymo’s 577.

thesis.title: Scale evidence
thesis.text: The first operational test is fleet size. Wolfe Research expects about 7,200 Robotaxi vehicles in 2026, while Tesla has disclosed manufacturing capacity rather than vehicles operating. Optimus needs outside deliveries by the end of 2027 and production capable of millions of robots annually.

valuePools.name: Robotaxi
valuePools.economics: 25% 2040 operating margin · USD 404bn 2040 operating profit · Morgan Stanley about USD 1tn 2040 opportunity
valuePools.text: Robotaxi is the largest component of the share price, carrying 309 USD per share. The price requires annual sales of USD 1.62tn by 2040, generated by fares from Tesla-operated fleets and software fees from other owners and operators. At a 25% operating margin, that produces USD 404bn of operating profit. The requirement exceeds Morgan Stanley’s roughly USD 1tn worldwide 2040 Robotaxi opportunity and is 1.6 times Goldman Sachs’s USD 415bn forecast for the whole market in 2035. Tesla began Cybercab rides in Austin on 3 September 2026 and reports nearly 2 million cumulative unsupervised miles, but Texas records listed only 42 authorised Tesla driverless vehicles in May 2026, versus 577 for Waymo. The share-price reading therefore turns on fleet growth, utilisation, permitting, cost per mile and software income.

valuePools.name: Optimus
valuePools.economics: 20% 2040 operating margin · USD 89.1bn 2040 operating profit · Roland Berger USD 750bn 2035 optimistic market
valuePools.text: Optimus carries 77 USD per share and requires annual robot sales of USD 445bn by 2040. A 20% operating margin would produce USD 89.1bn of operating profit. That sales requirement equals 2.8% of USD 15.7tn of US employee compensation and 1.7% of ARK Invest’s USD 26tn estimate of worldwide work available to humanoid robots. It also represents 24% of Roland Berger’s optimistic USD 750bn worldwide humanoid-sales scenario for 2035, while exceeding Goldman Sachs’s USD 138bn whole-market forecast. Production began on Tesla’s high-volume Fremont lines on 21 October 2026, but there is no announced commercial price, outside customer or confirmed delivery timetable. The evidence that matters is customer delivery by the end of 2027, weekly output, falling unit cost from UBS’s USD 50,000-60,000 estimate and sustained operating hours.

valuePools.name: Cars
valuePools.economics: 3.6x 2028 operating profit · USD 9,541m 2028 operating profit · peers 3.6x-3.7x
valuePools.text: Cars contributes 9 USD per share, based on a split of analysts’ forecast that gives the business USD 9,541m of 2028 operating profit on USD 127bn of sales and a 7% margin. The resulting 3.6x EV/EBIT is below the broader industry median of 7.1x and just below its lower quartile of 4.9x, but it matches General Motors at 3.6x and is close to Ford at 3.7x. The comparison is most relevant to those two traditional manufacturers because the wider median includes 27 profitable companies. Tesla sold USD 82.1bn to outside customers in 2025, produced 464,391 passenger vehicles in Q3 2026 and delivered 486,532, down 2% year on year. Battery availability limited volumes, while automotive gross margin was 18.5%, or 18.1% excluding regulatory credits.

valuePools.name: Energy
valuePools.economics: 10.4x 2028 operating profit · USD 1,485m 2028 operating profit · BYD 10.4x
valuePools.text: Energy contributes 4 USD per share, based on USD 1,485m of 2028 operating profit on USD 19.8bn of sales and a 7% margin. Its 10.4x EV/EBIT multiple is the same as BYD’s 2028 multiple and below the peer median of 11.4x, within an industry range of 9.2x to 16x. Energy sold USD 12.8bn to outside customers in 2025. Third-quarter 2026 revenue was USD 2,881m, down 16% year on year, against USD 1,927m of cost of revenue, while storage deployed rose 10% to 13.7 GWh. Tesla’s October update listed annual capacity of 50 GWh in Texas, 40 GWh in California and 20 GWh in Shanghai. The 7% margin depends on filling that capacity and avoiding tariff-related refunds; peer margins remain uneven, from Enphase’s 10.7% to SolarEdge’s -25.5%.

coreAnalysis.heading: What the price pays for
coreAnalysis.text: The share price is mostly a claim on businesses that barely sell anything yet. Cars and Energy together contribute 13 USD per share after applying 2028 peer EV/EBIT multiples to forecast operating profit of USD 9,541m and USD 1,485m respectively, then subtracting 2 USD per share for debt and other claims, less cash. Robotaxi contributes 309 USD per share and Optimus 77 USD per share. For Robotaxi, the required endpoint is USD 1.62tn of 2040 sales and USD 404bn of operating profit at a 25% margin. For Optimus, it is USD 445bn of sales and USD 89.1bn of operating profit at a 20% margin. Together the new businesses account for 386 USD per share. The whole-company bridge requires USD 2.41tn of 2040 sales and USD 519bn of operating profit, compared with USD 147bn of sales and USD 11bn of operating profit in 2028 forecasts. The implication is direct: the share price is made chiefly by the scale, margins and timing of Robotaxi and Optimus, not by the established Cars and Energy earnings base.

coreAnalysis.heading: Why the price differs from peers
coreAnalysis.text: Cars and Energy do not carry the same market reading. Cars costs 3.6x 2028 operating profit, matching General Motors at 3.6x and sitting close to Ford at 3.7x, while the broader profitable-company median is 7.1x. That lower multiple depends on reaching USD 127bn of 2028 sales and a 7% operating margin from USD 82.1bn of 2025 external sales. Energy costs 10.4x 2028 operating profit, matching BYD and sitting below the peer median of 11.4x. Its 7% forecast margin is neither a clear leader nor an outlier in a group ranging from Enphase’s 10.7% in 2025 to SolarEdge’s -25.5%. The whole company, however, trades at 277x 2026 forecast EV/EBIT and 143x 2028 forecast EV/EBIT because current and forecast established-business profits are small relative to the equity value of USD 1.57tn. The relevant comparison is therefore not a single blended peer multiple: established businesses have identifiable peer anchors, while most of the share price depends on future operating evidence from two new businesses.

coreAnalysis.heading: What to watch
coreAnalysis.text: The earliest evidence concerns physical scale. Robotaxi needs a fleet that can expand beyond six cities, with a disclosed vehicle count, annual sales and cost per paid mile. Tesla has nearly 2 million unsupervised miles and 42 authorised Texas vehicles, compared with Waymo’s 577 authorised vehicles and more than 500,000 paid trips a week. Wolfe Research expects about 7,200 Tesla vehicles in 2026, making a materially lower disclosure a warning. Optimus needs outside customers by the end of 2027, weekly production approaching Musk’s 20,000-robot marker and unit costs moving from UBS’s USD 50,000-60,000 estimate towards USD 20,000-30,000 at scale. Cars need deliveries to recover after Q3 2026’s 486,532 vehicles, battery supply to ease and automotive gross margin to hold near 18.5%. Energy needs Texas capacity to fill after production began, with storage deployment and revenue widening the USD 2,881m versus USD 1,927m third-quarter gap. These indicators determine whether the price’s business split is supported by operating progress.

risks: Robotaxi fleet shortfall (Robotaxi): a vehicle count materially below Wolfe Research’s 7,200 expectation would weaken the route to USD 1.62tn of 2040 sales, with authorised fleet size as the early warning.
Robotaxi economics (Robotaxi): low utilisation, vehicle, energy, insurance and support costs could prevent a 25% operating margin, with cost per paid mile as the early warning.

Optimus customer delay (Optimus): deliveries may not begin by the end of 2027 because AI, electromechanical design, reliability and operating life still need work, with outside-customer deliveries as the early warning.
Automotive margin pressure (Cars): price cuts, higher costs or constrained batteries could prevent the 7% 2028 operating margin, with automotive gross margin below 18.5% as the early warning.

Energy capacity underuse (Energy): weak demand or recurring tariff-related refunds could leave new factories underabsorbed, with storage deployment and the USD 2,881m revenue versus USD 1,927m cost-of-revenue gap as the early warning.
catalysts: Robotaxi fleet disclosure (near-term, Robotaxi): a vehicle count near or above Wolfe Research’s 7,200 expectation would provide the first measurable scale evidence.

Robotaxi permitting and annual sales (near-term, Robotaxi): driverless approval in California, expansion beyond six cities or a separate annual sales figure would establish progress towards USD 70.6bn of 2030 sales.
Optimus customer deliveries (medium-term, Optimus): outside deliveries by the end of 2027 would show that the design and reliability problems are sufficiently resolved for commercial trials.
Fremont production and costs (medium-term, Optimus): reported weekly output and falling unit cost towards USD 20,000-30,000 would support the required USD 445bn of 2040 sales.
Storage utilisation (near-term, Energy): rising deployment and plant-level output from Texas would show whether 50 GWh of annual capacity can lift the 7% operating margin.

faqs.q: What is Tesla's share price made of?
faqs.a: The 397 USD share price assigns 309 USD per share to Robotaxi, 77 USD per share to Optimus, 9 USD per share to Cars and 4 USD per share to Energy, less 2 USD per share for debt and other claims, less cash.

faqs.q: Why does Tesla trade at different multiples across its businesses?
faqs.a: Cars implies 3.6x 2028 operating profit of USD 9,541m, matching General Motors at 3.6x and Ford at 3.7x. Energy implies 10.4x 2028 operating profit of USD 1,485m, matching BYD. Robotaxi and Optimus depend on 2040 operating outcomes rather than established earnings.

faqs.q: What do analysts expect for Tesla?
faqs.a: The mean of 43 analysts’ targets is 409 USD, with a range of 128-600 USD, sourced from MarketScreener. Analysts forecast 2028 sales of USD 147,049m, EBITDA of USD 26,661m and operating profit of USD 11,026m.

Robotaxi fleet size, annual sales, permitting and cost per paid mile are central. Optimus customer deliveries by the end of 2027, weekly production and unit costs also matter. Cars require delivery growth and an automotive gross margin near 18.5%, while Energy needs capacity utilisation and improving margins.

faqs.q: How does Valuatum's market report work?
faqs.a: The method holds analysts’ forecasts to 2028, values Cars and Energy using selected peer EV/EBIT multiples, and allocates the remaining share price to Robotaxi and Optimus. The price needs USD 2.41tn of 2040 sales and USD 519bn of operating profit; no target price or recommendation is provided.

sources: Primary data: Valuatum market report on Tesla, Inc. dated 27 October 2026 (397 USD share price, Robotaxi 309 USD per share, Optimus 77 USD per share, Cars 9 USD per share and Energy 4 USD per share).

Competitor context: General Motors 3.6x and Ford 3.7x 2028 EV/EBIT for Cars; BYD 10.4x 2028 EV/EBIT for Energy; Cars industry median 7.1x and Energy peer median 11.4x. The wider Energy peer margins are uneven, including Enphase at 10.7% and SolarEdge at -25.5%.

Market data: TSLA, 397 USD on 27 October 2026; analysts’ forecasts used are 2028 sales of USD 147,049m and operating profit of USD 11,026m, with the 409 USD consensus from 43 analysts sourced from MarketScreener.
